notes: Customer persona: B2B SaaS with public KB + private support docs; wants unified search across both.
Index scale: initial 1.2M short fragments (kb articles, chat transcripts, API docs). Expect ~2.5M in 12 months.
Traffic profile: high query volume during business hours, peak bursts up to 450 QPS; median query size small (~32 tokens), rerank typically top-10 candidates.
Architecture preference: hosted API for speed to market; open to Dedicated later if cost/throughput needs justify.
Latency targets: 99th percentile for top-10 rerank <= 200ms; p50 target <= 100ms.
Quality: prefer bi-encoder candidate retrieval + cross-encoder rerank to reduce false positives; developer wants control over rerank threshold.
Cost sensitivity: wants per-query cost model. Primary ask: estimate monthly token and embedding compute cost at 250 QPS sustained with 1.2M index.
POC metrics requested: recall@10, MRR, average token cost, token/sec per GPU, cache hit rate, cold-start penalty.
Notes from SE: warm KV/prefix caching and batching reduced token cost by ~30% in test; need more realistic traffic mix for final numbers.
Legal/security: SSO + SAML integration mandatory; audit logs for all inference requests required for compliance; EU-residency for subset of data.
Customer quote from 2026-02-03 demo: 'Search must feel instant for customers — anything over 300ms feels slow; cost can't blow up at scale.'
Open questions: how Redwood routes to cheaper model variants for low-priority queries; fallback behavior under capacity pressure.
Suggested next actions: run a 72-hour load-run at 250 QPS with mixed query distribution; produce cost projection for 250/400/500 QPS scenarios.
Internal action items: SE to prepare config for caching + quantized rerank model; AE to coordinate legal & residency clause draft.

notes_summary: Mid-market SaaS (Arbor Knowledge Hub) evaluating Redwood hosted API for KB search with embeddings + cross-encoder rerank. Moderate index (1.2M), high QPS (250 sustained, bursts up to 450). Main asks: p99/p95 latency SLAs, per-query cost at scale, EU data residency for subset. POC shows promising latency but needs run at production-like traffic. Legal and pricing are current blockers.
